chunks: Abu Qurra the narrator asked me to take him to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him). So I sought his permission, and he permitted me. He entered and asked him about the permissible and the forbidden, then said to him: 'Do you acknowledge that God is carried?'

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Every carried thing is acted upon, attributed to something other than itself, and in need. The word "carried" is a term of deficiency in expression, while "carrier" is an agent and is praiseworthy in expression. Similarly are the words of one who says "above" and "below" and "higher" and "lower". God has said: "And to God belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them" [7:180] — and He did not say in His books that He is the carried one; rather He said that He is the Carrier on land and sea, and the Upholder of the heavens and the earth lest they decline. The "carried" is that which is other than God, and never has anyone who believes in God and His Majesty been heard to say in their supplication: "O Carried One!"'

Abu Qurra said: 'But He said: "And above them eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord on that Day" [69:17], and He said: "Those who bear the Throne" [40:7].' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'The Throne is not God. The Throne is a name of knowledge and power — a throne in which everything exists. Then He attributed the carrying to others of His creation, because He subjugated His creation through the carrying of His Throne — and they carry His knowledge. And He created beings who glorify around His Throne, performing by His knowledge, and angels who record the deeds of His servants; and He subjugated the people of the earth through circumambulation around His House. And God settled upon the Throne as He said.'

The Throne, and those who carry it, and those around the Throne — God is their Carrier, their Preserver, the Upholder, the Standing One over every soul, above everything, and upon everything. He cannot be called "the carried" nor "the lower" as a standalone word without connection to something else, for that would corrupt the word and the meaning.

Abu Qurra said: 'Are you denying the report which states that when God is angry, His anger is known because the angels who carry the Throne feel its weight upon their shoulders and fall prostrate? And when the anger subsides, it becomes lighter and they return to their places.'

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Tell me about God, Blessed and Exalted — since He cursed Iblis until this day of yours, He has been angry with him; so when did He become pleased? And according to your description, He does not cease to be angry with him, with his followers, and with his supporters. How do you dare to describe your Lord with change from one state to another, and that what flows upon creatures flows upon Him? Glorified is He and Exalted — He does not decline along with those who decline, nor does He change with those who change, nor alter with those who alter. Those below Him are in His hand and His management; all of them are in need of Him, and He is needless of any besides Him.'

key_terms.الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى: The Most Beautiful Names — Quranic concept that God's names are attributes of praise; 'carried' is not among them
key_terms.الْحَامِلُ: The Carrier — the active agent; the Imam affirms God is the Carrier (sustainer) of all things
key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: The Throne — interpreted by the Imam as a name representing divine knowledge and power, not a literal physical throne
key_terms.الْمُمْسِكُ: The Upholder/Sustainer — one of God's active attributes, contrasted with the passive 'carried'
key_terms.تَنْزِيهٌ: Divine transcendence — the principle that God cannot be described with creaturely attributes
key_terms.سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى: Glorified and Exalted — a formula of divine transcendence used to conclude the Imam's argument
key_terms.مَحْمُولٌ: Carried — a passive participle implying being acted upon by another, which the Imam argues is impossible for God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about whether God can be described as 'carried' (محمول)?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS) engages in a theological debate with Abu Qurra, a Sunni hadith scholar, who asks whether God can be described as 'carried' (محمول). The Imam refutes this anthropomorphic concept through precise linguistic and rational analysis: the word 'carried' implies passivity, need, and dependence — attributes impossible for God. He explains that the Quranic references to the Throne being carried refer to the Throne as a locus of knowledge and power, not to God Himself. The Imam further dismantles the idea of God's anger causing physical heaviness to the angels carrying the Throne, demonstrating that attributing changing emotional states to God — like creatures — contradicts divine transcendence (tanzih). This dialogue reflects the theological milieu of Imam al-Rida's era (early 3rd century AH) when Mutazilite, Murji'ite, and various hadith-based traditions debated divine attributes vigorously at the Abbasid court.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya who said, 
‘Abu Qurra the narrator asked me if I could take him to see Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>. So I sought permission for him and he<sup>asws</sup> permitted it for me. So he came over and asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Permissible and the Prohibitions, then said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So do you<sup>asws</sup> acknowledge that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is carried?’

So Abu Al-Hassanasws said: ‘Every carried is performed with as an addition to something else, needy, and the carried is deficient regarding the word, and the carrier is the performer, and he is praiseworthy regarding the word; and similar to that are the words of the speaker, ‘Above’, and ‘Under’, and ‘Higher’, and ‘Lower’; and Allahazwj has Said [7:180] And Allah's are the Best Names, therefore call on Him by these, and did not Say in Hisazwj Books that Heazwj is the carried One. But Heazwj Said that Heazwj is the Carrier in the land and the sea and the Upholder of the skies and the earth lest they decline; and the carried is what is besides Allahazwj, and it is not heard from anyone who believes in Allahazwj and Hisazwj Magnificence at all that he says in his supplication, ‘O Carried One!’’.

Abu Qurra said, ‘But Heazwj Says [69:17] and above them eight shall bear on that Day the Throne of your Lord, and Said [40:7] Those who are bearing the Throne!’ So Abu Al-Hassanasws said: ‘The Throne (الْعَرْشَ), it is not Allahazwj, and the ‘Throne’ is a name of ‘Knowledge and Power’, and the Throne (الْعَرْشَ), in it is everything. Then Heazwj Supplemented the carriers to others Heazwj Created from Hisazwj creatures because Heazwj Enslaved Hisazwj by the carriers of Hisazwj Throne (الْعَرْشَ), and theyasws carry Hisazwj Knowledge, and creatures are Glorifying Him around Hisazwj Throne (الْعَرْشَ), and they are performing by Hisazwj Knowledge, and the Angels are recording the deeds of Hisazwj servants, and the people of the earth are worshipping by the Tawaaf around Hisazwj House (Kabah), and Allahazwj is Even upon the Throne (الْعَرْشِ), Even just as Heazwj Said.

And (as for) the Throne (الْعَرْشِ) and the ones who are carrying it, and the ones around the Throne (الْعَرْشِ), and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Carrier of them, the Preserver of them, the Upholder, the Standing One upon every soul, and above everything, and upon everything, and He<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be called ‘The Carried One’, nor by a lower solitary word, nor can He<sup>azwj</sup> be arrived to anything. So it would spoil the word and the meaning’.

Abu Qurra said, ‘So you<sup>asws</sup> are belying the report which have come that Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, when He<sup>azwj</sup> is Angry, rather His<sup>azwj</sup> Anger is recognised. The Angels who are carrying the Throne (الْعَرْشِ) are finding its weight upon their shoulders, so they fall down prostrate. So when the Anger subsides, it becomes lighter, and they return to their places’.

So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Inform me<sup>asws</sup> about Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High, since He<sup>azwj</sup> Cursed Iblees<sup>la</sup> up to this day of yours, He<sup>azwj</sup> is Angry upon him<sup>la</sup>, so when is He<sup>azwj</sup> Pleased, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is in your description, does not cease to be Angry upon him<sup>la</sup> and upon his<sup>la</sup> followers. How can you be so audacious that you are describing your Lord<sup>azwj</sup> with the alteration from a state to a state, and that it flows upon Him<sup>azwj</sup> what flows upon the creatures?
Glorious is He<sup>azwj</sup> and Exalted, not declining along with the decliners, and does not alter with the altering ones, and does not change with the changing ones, and the ones besides Him<sup>azwj</sup> are in His<sup>azwj</sup> Hands, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Management, and all of them are needy to Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Needless from the ones besides Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya who has said the following. “Abu Qurrah, the narrator of Hadith asked for help to meet Imam Ali abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.). I requested the Imam (a.s.) to meet him and he agreed. Abu Qurrah asked the Imam about the lawful and unlawful matters and then said, “Do you affirm that Allah is carried?”

Imam abu al-Hassan (a.s.) replied, “Every thing in an objective case is related to another thing and is dependent. Being carried is the name for verbal defect. On the other hand, carrier is in a subjective case and it verbally is a word to convey praises and so is the expression of one who says, “Above, below, upper and lower.” Allah has said, ‘For Him there are beautiful names, thus, call Him through those names.’ He (Allah) has not said anywhere in His books that He is al-Mahmul (Being carried) He has, in fact, said that He is the carrier in the sea and on land and the preserver of the heavens and earth from banishment. Al-Mahmul, (being carried) are things other than Allah. It is never heard from any one who believed in Allah and His greatness saying in his prayers Ya Mahmul, (O the one being carried,).”

Abu Qurrah then said, “He Himself has said, ‘The angels will be around the heavens and on that day eight of them will carry the Throne of your Lord above all the creatures.’ [69:17] Also He has said, “Those who carry the Throne (al-‘Arsh).” Imam abu al-Hassan (a.s.) then said, “Al-‘Arsh (the Throne) is not Allah. Al-‘Arsh is the name of knowledge and power. In al-‘Arsh there is everything. Besides, He has ascribed carrying to things other than His Own-self. It is ascribed to a creature among His creatures. This is because He has made His creatures to worship Him through carrying His al-‘Arsh (the Throne) and they are the carrier of His knowledge. There is a creature, who speaks of His praise around His al-‘Arsh (the Throne) and act according to His knowledge and the angels write down the deeds of His servants. He has made those on earth to worship Him in the form of Tawaf (walking around) His house. Allah has control over al-‘Arsh (the Throne) as He has said,

“Allah carries al-‘Arsh, those who carry it and those around it, preserves them, keeps them together and is the guardian of all souls and above and over all things.” It is not permissible to say, “He is carried. He is below.” It would be the only expression that would not make any sense. Thus, both the word and meaning would be destroyed.”

Abu Qurrah than said, “Do you then consider a false Hadith the Hadith that says, “When Allah becomes angry His anger becomes known to the angels who carry al-‘Arsh. They at such time feel the weight of His anger on their shoulders. They then bow down in prostration. When Allah’s anger goes away it becomes light and the angels return to their places.”

Imam abu al-Hassan (a.s.) said, “Tell me about Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High. From the time He condemned Satan until today is He not angry with Satan? When did He become happy with Satan? As you say He is still angry with Satan, his friend and followers. How would you dare speak of your Lord as under going changes from one condition to another condition and that what happens to the creatures happens to Him also. He is the Most Glorious, the Most High. He does not banish with those who banish and does not change with those who change. He is not replaced with those who are replaced. The creatures are under His guardianship and they all are dependent on Him. He is Self-sufficient and independent of others.”
